{"description":"Scenario: a caller wires up SCT verification for TLS server cert validation. They get back `count = 0`. They have no way to distinguish:
- All SCTs were signed by logs the caller does not trust (UnknownLog).
- All SCTs had timestamps outside the log window (SctTimestampOutsideLogWindow).
- All SCTs had signatures that failed cryptographic verification (InvalidSignature) — this is the SECURITY-SIGNIFICANT case.
- The log key was malformed (LogKeyMalformed) — corrupted trust state.
- The cert DER was too long (CertDerTooLong) — impossible in practice.

These have wildly different security implications. "InvalidSignature" suggests a CT log signing-key compromise or a forged SCT — a serious alarm. "UnknownLog" suggests the caller's log list is stale — a configuration issue. The library MERGES these into the same zero-count outcome.

Maintenance consequence: every user filing 'why does my cert show zero valid SCTs?' will produce a long support thread because pkix-ct returns no diagnostic. The doc comment (verify.rs:357-364) admits this is intentional ('count vs policy threshold'), but the design is wrong: a verifier that drops error information is hostile to debugging.

Fix options:
1. Return `Vec<(usize, Result<&CtLog>)>` indexed by SCT position, letting callers inspect each one. Most flexible.
2. Add a sibling `verify_embedded_scts_detailed` that returns the same. Keep `verify_embedded_scts` as a thin wrapper for the common case.
3. At minimum, add a `tracing::debug!` per failure. Cheap, prelaunch-acceptable.

Architectural-completeness note (per AGENTS.md 'project phase'): the workspace is prelaunch. The complete shape for SCT verification is 'caller sees per-SCT verdict.' Shipping a count-only API now will fossilize into a permanent maintenance footgun. Breaking changes are free pre-1.0; design closure means picking the right shape now.

Provenance: filed as PKIX-ppbr.6 on 2026-05-14, re-filed as PKIX-d4h.8 on 2026-06-15 with the description reduced to a pointer. PKIX-ppbr.6 is closed; this bead now carries its analysis verbatim."}

Fixed, additively. The per-SCT error was being discarded by `.is_ok()`, so every failure reached the caller as the same empty vector.

Added verify_embedded_scts_with_report -> EmbeddedSctReport { verified: Vec<VerifiedSct>, rejected: Vec<RejectedSct> }, where RejectedSct carries log_id, timestamp_ms and reason: Error. The five outcomes the bead listed -- UnknownLog, SctTimestampOutsideLogWindow, InvalidSignature, LogKeyMalformed, CertDerTooLong -- are now each reported as themselves.

Deliberately NOT a breaking change. verify_embedded_scts keeps its signature and becomes a thin wrapper returning the reports verified half, and count_embedded_sct_logs is untouched. Both rustdocs now say to use the report wherever the zero case will be acted on or logged. The bead said "the design is wrong"; the design that was wrong was discarding the reason, not the existence of a count-shaped convenience, so the convenience stays and the information is no longer destroyed to produce it.

Naming follows the workspace precedent, pkix-truststore-system::from_system_with_report, rather than inventing a second convention.

Details worth keeping:

- Both halves can be non-empty at once. Three good SCTs and one with a bad signature is a certificate worth a second look, and a caller counting only successes never sees it. The old shape could not express this at all.
- RejectedSct::log_id and timestamp_ms are documented as CLAIMED, not verified. On an InvalidSignature rejection nothing in the struct has been authenticated, so it is a lead for an operator, not a fact to act on. Not noting that would have been a new trap in place of the old one.
- Duplicates stay out of `rejected`. Dedup runs before verification, so a second SCT from an already-verified log is skipped; reporting it as a rejection would make a well-formed certificate read as partly broken.
- VerifiedSct gained the serde derives it was missing (EmbeddedSctReport needs them, and Error and CtLog already had them). A report is exactly what a deployment wants to serialize and log.

Test: the two pre-existing zero-count tests, returns_zero_when_logs_empty and returns_zero_when_issuer_wrong, assert nothing but an empty vector -- this bug written down as coverage. The new test reuses their own fixtures and asserts the PAIR differs, UnknownLog against InvalidSignature, because either case alone cannot demonstrate that they are distinguishable. A second test pins that a fully successful verification leaves rejected empty and that the wrapper still equals the reports verified half. Verified by mutation: restoring the discard makes the first test fail with left: [] against right: [UnknownLog].

Gates: fmt, clippy, rustdoc, 2376 workspace tests, pkix-ct feature powerset.
